display.title: Bringing Nachas to Your Parents: A Girl's Own Shabbos Candle
display.summary_short: Children are their parents' greatest treasure and repay them with nachas by honoring them; a special way for girls is lighting their own Shabbos candle beside their mother.
display.summary_long: A talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. Uncle Yossi tells children that they are the most precious treasure their parents have: their father works and their mother cooks and cares for them so they will grow up happy. What do we owe them in return? Nachas, which comes through honoring father and mother as Hashem commanded in the Ten Commandments. He then shows a special way for girls to do this. The Torah compares mitzvos to a candle and Torah to light, because light lets us see what is good and what is harmful, and the more we learn and do, the more light we have. The one mitzvah whose light we can actually see is the Shabbos candle, lit eighteen minutes before sunset. Every girl old enough to know that Shabbos is coming can light her own candle beside her mother, and nothing gives a mother more nachas than hearing her daughter's brachah.
display.lesson: Bring your parents nachas by honoring them; girls can light their own Shabbos candle beside their mother.
